result:
The helper and its tests are done, and I'm accepting the change after one executor round-trip.

**What was added**
- `src/mem_mcp/util_text.py` adds `slugify_title(title: str) -> str`. It lowercases and trims the title, turns each run of characters outside ASCII `[a-z0-9]` into a single `-`, and strips hyphens from both ends. The pattern is deliberately ASCII-only, so non-ASCII letters are dropped, which the task allows. The module follows `CONVENTIONS.md`: it has `from __future__ import annotations`, full type hints, docstrings, and a regex compiled once at module level.
- `tests/unit/test_util_text.py` has 14 plain pytest tests covering:
  - normal text and whitespace trimming
  - punctuation runs, and punctuation at the start or end
  - digits being kept
  - empty, whitespace-only and punctuation-only input, which all give `""`
  - unicode: `"Café Déjà Vu"` gives `"caf-d-j-vu"` and `"日本語"` gives `""`
  - running the function on its own output leaves it unchanged

No other files changed; `git status` shows only the two new files.

**Verification**
- I couldn't run the checks myself because my pytest command needed an approval it didn't get. The executor reports these results:
  - `pytest tests/unit/test_util_text.py -q`: 14 passed
  - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean
  - `mypy` (strict): no issues
- I read both files and traced the logic and each expected test value by hand; they agree with the spec.

**Remaining concerns:** None beyond running the tests myself. I'm highly confident the acceptance criteria are met.
